title: The Birth of the Prophet ﷺ and His Upbringing in the Desert
overview: This episode covers the marriage of the Prophet's ﷺ parents, Abdullah and Aminah, the passing of Abdullah prior to his son's birth, and the remarkable events surrounding the birth of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in the Year of the Elephant. It detail signs of prophethood manifested across Arabia and Persia, the story behind his naming, and the Quraysh custom of sending infants to the desert. Finally, it highlights the immense blessings (barakah) experienced by Halimah al-Sa'diyyah upon fostering the young Prophet ﷺ.
lessons: Seeking divine blessing (barakah) through good deeds yields far greater rewards than chasing immediate material gain, as demonstrated by Halimah taking an orphan child when others refused.
Allah prepares His chosen servants with pure character and honorable backgrounds, ensuring the Prophet ﷺ was born into the most respectable lineage of Arabia.
Divine protection and decree are at work even before a person's mission begins, illustrated by the miraculous preservation of Abdullah and the signs preceding the Prophet's ﷺ birth.
The importance of environment in shaping speech, health, and fortitude, as seen in the Quraysh practice of raising children in the desert to instill resilience and linguistic purity.

chapters.title: Lineage and Marriage of the Prophet's Parents
chapters.summary: The lecture begins by recalling how Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib was spared from sacrifice when one hundred camels were offered in his place, fulfilling the Prophet's statement that he was 'the son of the two slaughtered ones' (Ismail and Abdullah). Abdul Muttalib arranged for Abdullah to marry Aminah bint Wahb, an honorable woman from Yathrib who shared descent from Abd Manaf. Their marriage took place in Yathrib before they returned to Makkah. Shortly after Aminah became pregnant, Abdullah passed away, leaving the Prophet ﷺ an orphan before birth.
key_points: The Prophet ﷺ referred to himself as 'the son of the two slaughtered ones' (Ismail and Abdullah)
Marriage of Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib and Aminah bint Wahb in Yathrib
Shared noble lineage through Abd Manaf back to Ismail (alayhis-salam)
Passing of Abdullah during Aminah's pregnancy, leaving Rasulullah ﷺ an orphan prior to birth

chapters.title: Dreams of Aminah and the Birth of Rasulullah ﷺ
chapters.summary: As the time of delivery approached, Aminah experienced extraordinary dreams, including a light issuing from her that illuminated the palaces of Busra in Sham. She was also instructed in a dream to seek Allah's protection for her newborn from every envier. According to the most authentic view, Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was born on Monday, the 12th of Rabi al-Awwal in the Year of the Elephant (Am al-Fil), fifty days after the miraculous destruction of Abrahah's army.
key_points: Aminah's dream of an illuminating light reaching Busra in Sham
Dream instruction to seek Allah's protection against jealous enviers
Birth date on Monday, 12th of Rabi al-Awwal in the Year of the Elephant (Am al-Fil)
Birth occurred fifty days after the destruction of Abrahah and his army

chapters.title: Signs at Birth and Abdul Muttalib's Gratitude
chapters.summary: In Madinah, Hassan ibn Thabit recalled witnessing a Jewish monk stand atop a structure to announce the appearance of Ahmad's star on the day of birth. Aminah enjoyed an unusually light and easy pregnancy without normal discomforts. Narrations record that the Prophet ﷺ was born circumcised and with his umbilical cord already detached. Overjoyed by these miraculous signs, Abdul Muttalib carried his newborn grandson inside the Ka'bah to thank Allah, proclaiming that the child had a magnificent future.
key_points: Jewish monk in Madinah announcing the emergence of Ahmad's star, witnessed by young Hassan ibn Thabit
Aminah's effortless pregnancy compared to usual maternal hardship
Physical signs at birth: born circumcised with the umbilical cord detached
Abdul Muttalib's prayer inside the Ka'bah declaring 'Inna li-ibni hadha la-sha'nan'

chapters.title: The Naming of Muhammad ﷺ and Portents in Persia
chapters.summary: Abdul Muttalib chose the rare name Muhammad after a trip to Sham where a Jewish monk informed him and three companions that a prophet bearing that name would arise in Arabia. At the moment of the Prophet's ﷺ birth, extraordinary portents struck the Persian Empire: the sacred fire of the Majus was extinguished, an earthquake damaged Kisra's palace causing fourteen balconies to collapse, and Lake Sawah suddenly dried up. Troubled, Kisra consulted fortune-tellers who foretold that only fourteen kings would remain in his dynasty, ten of whom ruled within just four years.
key_points: Origin of the name Muhammad from Abdul Muttalib's encounter with a Jewish monk in Sham
Extinguishing of the sacred fire worshipped by the Majus in Persia
Earthquake destroying fourteen balconies of King Kisra's palace and the drying up of Lake Sawah
Prediction of fortune-tellers that only fourteen Persian kings remained before the fall of their empire

chapters.title: The Quraysh Custom of Desert Upbringing
chapters.summary: The Quraysh followed a customary practice of sending infant boys away from Makkah to be raised by Bedouin foster mothers in the desert. This tradition served three key purposes: mastering pure, uncorrupted Arabic (fus'ha) away from non-native urban speech, developing physical strength and masculine toughness, and avoiding diseases spread by international pilgrims visiting Makkah. Foster mothers came to Makkah periodically, relying on voluntary gifts of gratitude from fathers rather than negotiating fixed upfront fees.
key_points: Three main reasons for desert upbringing: pure Arabic dialect (fus'ha), physical fortitude, and avoiding city diseases
Linguistic impact of non-Arab pilgrims settling in Makkah on the local dialect
Cultural etiquette of wet nurses accepting infants without setting fixed upfront fees
Custom of fathers presenting generous gifts to foster mothers upon returning children

chapters.title: Halimah al-Sa'diyyah and the Barakah of Taking the Prophet ﷺ
chapters.summary: Halimah al-Sa'diyyah and her husband al-Harith from Banu Sa'd arrived in Makkah during a period of famine, riding a weak, slow donkey. Other wet nurses rejected the infant Muhammad ﷺ because he was fatherless and they feared minimal monetary reward. Having found no other child, Halimah decided to take the orphan in hopes of divine blessing (barakah). Miracles occurred immediately: her weak donkey outpaced the entire caravan on the journey back, and her milk became instantly abundant to feed both her own infant and Muhammad ﷺ.
key_points: Halimah al-Sa'diyyah and al-Harith of the tribe of Banu Sa'd
Rejection of the orphan Prophet ﷺ by other wet nurses due to lack of fatherly compensation
Halimah's decision to accept him seeking divine barakah
Immediate miracles: dramatic speed of the weak donkey and sudden abundance of milk

segments.translit: Bismillāhi r-Raḥmāni r-Raḥīm. Al-ḥamdu lillāhi Rabbi l-ʿālamīn. Wa-ṣallallāhu wa-sallama wa-bāraka ʿalā nabiyyinā Muḥammadin wa-ʿalā ālihi wa-ṣaḥbihi ajmaʿīn. Rabbi shraḥ lī ṣadrī wa-yassir lī amrī wa-ḥlul ʿuqdatam min lisānī yafqahū qawlī. Allāhumma ʿallimnā mā yanfaʿunā wa-nfaʿnā bimā ʿallamtanā wa-zidnā ʿilmā.

segments.text: [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]] today we will start where we left off last week, when we spoke about the father of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله بن عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]],
and how Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] saved him from being slaughtered. And we spoke about that story last week,
how the father of Abdullah, [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], who is the grandfather of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, how he had vowed that if he had ten sons, that he would sacrifice one of them.
But then in the end, instead of doing that, he sacrificed one hundred camels. And [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله بن عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], the father of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, was saved.
And that is why the Prophet ﷺ said: '[[Ana ibnudh-dhabihayn|أنا ابن الذبيحين]] - I am the son of the two who were about to be slaughtered.'
And that would be [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]] and Abdullah, the father of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ.
So Abdullah was saved in this way, and a hundred camels were sacrificed instead.
And when Abdullah grew up, he was the most beloved son to his father. He was the most beloved son to [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]].
So when he became of an age where he was ready to get married, [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] wanted him to marry the best woman.
So he decided to marry his son to [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة بنت وهب]]. And [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة بنت وهب]], who is the mother of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ,
she also came from a very pure and respectable and honorable lineage.
And she also was from the descendants of [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]]. As we mentioned earlier that the Prophet ﷺ and his lineage,
he is Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] ibn [[Hashim|هَاشِم]] ibn [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]] ibn [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]].
So [[Abd Manaf|عَبْد مَنَاف]] was one of the sons of [[Qusayy ibn Kilab|قُصَيّ بن كِلَاب]], and [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ's lineage goes back to him
from the father's side, and also from the mother's side.

So both [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله بن عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] and [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة بنت وهب]], the parents of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, they were from a very high and respectable lineage from the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]],
and they were both from the children, the descendants of [[Ismail|إسماعيل]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]]. So the Prophet ﷺ was born into the most honorable lineage.
His family tree is the most honorable lineage.
So when [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] wanted his son to get married, he decided to marry him to [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة بنت وهب]].

Now [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة بنت وهب]], she lived with her family in [[Yathrib|يثرب]]. They didn't live in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], they lived in [[Yathrib|يثرب]]. And [[Yathrib|يثرب]], of course, would later on
become to be known as [[al-Madinah al-Nabawiyyah|الْمَدِينَة النَّبَوِيَّة]], the city of the Prophet ﷺ, because that is eventually where he made [[Hijrah|هِجْرَة]] to.
But at that time, it was not called [[Madinah|مدينة]], it was called [[Yathrib|يثرب]].
And that is where the mother of the Prophet ﷺ, [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة بنت وهب]], and her family, they used to live there in [[Yathrib|يثرب]].
So when the marriage was agreed upon, [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] took his son Abdullah to [[Yathrib|يثرب]], and the marriage took place in [[Yathrib|يثرب]].
So the marriage of the parents of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ was done in [[Yathrib|يثرب]]. And then after the marriage, they returned to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
So Abdullah, with his new wife Aminah, they came from [[Madinah|مدينة]] to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]. And shortly after the marriage, Aminah, she became pregnant.
And Abdullah, the father of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, died just a few months into his wife's pregnancy.
So when [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله بن عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] died, his wife [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة بنت وهب]] was pregnant with [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ.
So the father of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ died even before he was born. So [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ was an orphan even before his birth.
Now when the time of the birth of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ came near, now Aminah, she is in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
So when the time of the birth of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ came near, Aminah, she saw a dream. She saw a dream that she's giving birth to this boy,
and along with this boy, a great light is coming out, an illuminating light that illuminates the earth,
and it can be seen all the way up to Busra in [[Sham|شام]]. So with this boy, this great illumination is coming out.
She also saw in a dream that she was saying about this boy who was being born:

segments.translit: Uʿīdhuhu bi-Llāhi l-Wāḥid min sharri kulli ḥāsid

segments.text: I seek the protection of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] for this boy.
I seek the protection of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], the One, for this boy, from the evil of every jealous person.
So even though the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], they were [[mushrikin|مشركين]], they used to worship idols and they used to associate partners with Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], in her dream,
she is seeking refuge in Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] alone for this boy.
So these were some of the dreams that she saw near the time that [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ was born.
And then on the twelfth of [[Rabi al-Awwal|ربيع الأول]], in the Year of the Elephant, [[Am al-Fil|عام الفيل]],
and the [[Am al-Fil|عام الفيل]], we spoke about that before, that was the year that the incident happened where [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] came from [[Yemen|اليمن]] to destroy the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]],
and how Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] destroyed [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] and his army, and He protected His house, He protected the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
So that was the year where [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ was born. On the twelfth of [[Rabi al-Awwal|ربيع الأول]], according to the most authentic opinion.
And there is some [[ikhtilaf|اختلاف]] on the date of his birth,

not all of the [[ulama|علماء]] are agreed that he was born on the twelfth of [[Rabi al-Awwal|ربيع الأول]], but perhaps it is the strongest opinion that he was born on Monday, the twelfth of [[Rabi al-Awwal|ربيع الأول]].
Surely he was born on a Monday, but there is some [[ikhtilaf|اختلاف]] about the date, was it the twelfth of [[Rabi al-Awwal|ربيع الأول]] or another date.
But the most authentic opinion [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]] is that it was the twelfth of [[Rabi al-Awwal|ربيع الأول]].

So on Monday, the twelfth of [[Rabi al-Awwal|ربيع الأول]], in [[Am al-Fil|عام الفيل]], the Year of the Elephant, the year that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] destroyed [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] and his army,
the greatest man who ever walked on the earth was born. And this happened fifty days after the incident of [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] and his army.
Fifty days after Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] destroyed [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] and his army, the Prophet ﷺ was born.
So this was one of the great events in the history of mankind, the birth of the greatest creation of Allah, [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ.
were settled in [[Madinah|الْمَدِينَة]]. So [[Hassan ibn Thabit|حَسَّان بن ثَابِت]], he was sitting with the Jews of [[Madinah|الْمَدِينَة]],
when one of the monks of the Jews came up and stood on one of their structures, and he announced,

segments.translit: Qad ẓahara al-yawm najmu Aḥmad, alladhī lā yaẓharu illā bi-khurūjih.
Qad ẓahara al-yawm najmu Aḥmad, alladhī lā yaẓharu illā bi-khurūjih.

segments.text: And [[Hassan ibn Thabit|حَسَّان بن ثَابِت]], he remembers this incident and he witnessed it personally when he was seven years old in [[Madinah|الْمَدِينَة]].
This Jewish monk climbed up on the structure and he said, "Today, the star of [[Ahmad|أَحْمَد]] has come out."
And it is a star that is never seen and could not be seen until this prophet comes.
And the Jews, they knew about the Prophet ﷺ, and they were awaiting a prophet to come.
And their book, the [[Tawrah|تَوْرَاة]], it had many descriptions of [[Rasulullah|رَسُول الله]] ﷺ in their book. So they knew that a prophet was about to come.
So one day, this man, he climbed up the structure and he said this: [[Qad zahara al-yawm najmu Ahmad alladhi la yazharu illa bi-khurujih|قد ظهر اليوم نجم أحمد الذي لا يظهر إلا بخروجه]].
Today the star of [[Ahmad|أَحْمَد]] has come out, and this star does not come out or would not come out except when this prophet is born.
So that means the Prophet ﷺ has been born.
So [[Hassan ibn Thabit|حَسَّان بن ثَابِت]] mentions this incident that he personally witnessed himself.
Also, another sign is that the pregnancy of [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة]] with [[Rasulullah|رَسُول الله]] ﷺ was a very easy pregnancy.
She didn't have any difficulties or any problems during that pregnancy. It went very easily the whole time.
When, usually, pregnancy is something that is very difficult for a woman, as Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] says in the Quran:
The mother of insan, the mother of a man carries the baby with difficulty and gives birth to the baby also with difficulty. It's not an easy thing.
But the pregnancy of [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة]] with her son [[Rasulullah|رَسُول الله]] ﷺ was a very easy pregnancy, and she didn't have any type of difficulties at all.
Also, it has been said that when [[Rasulullah|رَسُول الله]] ﷺ was born, he was born already circumcised.
Usually when a boy is born, then you circumcise him after his birth.
But [[Rasulullah|رَسُول الله]] ﷺ, according to this narration, was born already circumcised and he was also born with the umbilical cord already detached.
And usually when a baby is born, the doctor or whoever is assisting in the birth, they have to cut the umbilical cord.
But [[Rasulullah|رَسُول الله]] ﷺ was born with the umbilical cord already detached. So born circumcised, born with the umbilical cord already detached,
these are some signs that this boy is someone who is special. This is not a normal type of birth.
So when the grandfather of [[Rasulullah|رَسُول الله]] ﷺ, when [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] heard about this, that yes, [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة]] has given birth, her son has been born,
and these were the incidents that took place at his birth: he was born circumcised, he was born with the umbilical cord already detached,
then [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], he knew, he knew that this is something special. This is not just an average boy.
And he said, "[[Wallahi|وَاللَّهِ]] [[inna li-ibni hadha la-sha'nan|إِنَّ لِابْنِي هَذَا لَشَأْنًا]]."
By Allah, surely this son of mine, this boy of mine is something special and he will have something very special in his future. This is not just a normal boy.
So he realized that, and he took his grandson, and his grandson was not named yet. He was not named [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] yet.
So he took his grandson and he took him inside the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]].
He held him and he took him inside the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]], and he thanked Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] for blessing him with this grandson.
Now, what about the name of [[Rasulullah|رَسُول الله]] ﷺ? How did he get the name [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]]?
[[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] was not a name among the Arabs at that time. There was no one named [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]]. But [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], he named his grandson [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]].
And what is the reason behind this name?
Before, [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] had traveled to [[Sham|شَام]], the greater Syria area. [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] was on a trip to [[Sham|شَام]] with three of his companions.
So [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] and three other companions of his were there in [[Sham|شَام]].
And while they were in [[Sham|شَام]], they met with a Jewish monk, and they got involved in a conversation, [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] and his three companions with this Jewish monk.
So the Jewish monk asked [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] and the companions of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], "Where are you guys from?" And then they answered, "From [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]."

And then the Jewish monk, who had knowledge of the previous scriptures, he had knowledge of the [[Tawrah|تَوْرَاة]], and he had knowledge of the religion of [[Musa|مُوسَى]] [[alayhis-salam|عَلَيْهِ السَّلَام]],
so he said to [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] and his companions, "That place where you are from, the [[Jazirat al-Arab|جَزِيرَة الْعَرَب]], a prophet is going to come from there.
A prophet is going to come from there."
So they said, "Really? What is that prophet's name going to be? What is his name going to be?"
And then the Jewish monk replied, "His name is going to be [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]]. His name is going to be [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]]."
So from that instant, [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] and those three companions who were with him, they decided: if we ever get any son born in our family,
we are going to name him [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]], in hope that he would be that messenger.
So they all made this intention that the first son that would come in their family, they would name him [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]].
Now [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], he was old and he was not going to have any more sons, so he decided instead to name this name to his grandson.
And the other three companions of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], when they had a son, they also named their children [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]].
And [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], he named his grandson [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]]. So that is how he got the name of [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]]. And surely, he did become the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
And it was a name that was not used by the Arabs, nobody had this name. But [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], he gave this name to his grandson, [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ.
There were also some other great events, amazing incidents that happened when the Prophet ﷺ was born.

One of those incidents was that the fire in Persia that was worshipped by the [[Majus|مَجُوس]]—the [[Majus|مَجُوس]], they were the fire-worshippers and they had a fire that they used to worship—when the Prophet ﷺ was born, that fire extinguished.

Also, a great earthquake rattled Persia and rattled the palace of the [[Kisra|كِسْرَى]], who was the king of Persia, and he was the most powerful king in the world at that time, the [[Kisra|كِسْرَى]] of Persia.
So this big earthquake hit Persia, it hit his palace and the palace was damaged, and 14 balconies of that palace fell down. 14 balconies of that palace fell down.
Also, there was a lake that the Persians used to consider holy, and the name of that lake was Sawah.
And when that earthquake happened, the earth from underneath that lake opened up, and the river disappeared as well. That river or that lake was obliterated.
So they lost that lake, the palace was damaged, 14 balconies fell down, and the fire that the [[Majus|مَجُوس]] used to worship, that was also extinguished.
So these are some of the things that happened when the Prophet ﷺ was born.
And the [[Kisra|كِسْرَى]] of Persia, seeing all of this, he got scared, he got worried: what's happening here? These things happening all at the same time: the fire is extinguished,
the balconies of the palace fall down, the lake disappears. This is something. He was afraid.
So he called the fortune tellers to consult them about what is this, what is going on here.
And these fortune tellers, some of them used to have connections with the [[jinn|جن]].

Some of these fortune tellers, they used to have connection with the [[jinn|جن]], and as Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] mentions about these fortune tellers and the [[jinn|جن]]s that they used:
that these [[jinn|جن]]s, they used to go up into the sky and they used to try to eavesdrop to listen to any information that is being relayed there in the skies.
And then they would come down to earth and they would...
would give this information to the fortune tellers, and the fortune tellers would give this information to the people. And this was a big fitnah,
this fortune telling.
So the fortune tellers came to the [[Kisra|كسرى]] when he called them to come, and he asked them,
you know, what what is the meaning, what is the significance of these incidents that have happened?
The fire has been extinguished, this big earthquake came, the lake is gone, 14 balconies have fallen down from our palace.
What is the significance of this? So the fortune tellers told him, it means that there is a [[Nabi|نبي]] coming, that there is going to be a prophet,
a prophet is coming. And then the [[Kisra|كسرى]] said, "Okay, so what about the 14 balconies that fell down? What is the significance of that?" And they told him
that it means that there will be only 14 more kings in your empire. There will be 14 [[Kisra|كسرى]]s,
and after the 14th one, the kingdom of Persia, the Persian Empire will be gone. You have 14 left in your line of kingship,
14 people. So then the [[Kisra|كسرى]], he felt a little bit relaxed, he felt comfortable. He said, "Oh, 14? 14 kings? Okay,
that's still a long time.
That's still a very long time." But what happened when the [[Kisra|كسرى]] died, when this [[Kisra|كسرى]] died?
The other members of the royal family, they fought over the rule.
It was not a peaceful transition of power. So in the next four years, there were 10 kings.
In the next four years, there were 10 kings out of those 14. So the time was coming very near.
Now, back to the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] and back to the birth of the Prophet ﷺ, the habit of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]]
is that they wouldn't like to raise their children in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] from a young age.
They wouldn't let, they wouldn't want them to have their initial upbringing in the city of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] itself.
Rather, they would send them out into the desert so that they could grow up there. And there were many reasons for this. One of the reasons
was that [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] was a place where people from all over used to come. People from all different lands, they used to come to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] for [[Hajj|حج]].
And many of those people, when they would come to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] and do [[Hajj|حج]], they wouldn't leave, they would just stay there. Now, these people,
they were from different backgrounds, they were from different cultures, and they spoke different languages.
They spoke different languages, but when they were settling themselves in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], they had to learn Arabic.
So they learned it, but they were not that fluent in it.
So that affected the actual people of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] as well. The fact that there were so many outsiders
who didn't speak Arabic fluently staying in that city, it affected the locals as well. The children, when they would grow up,
they would have to associate with all of these people who come from all over the place with different languages.
So they would try to speak to them in Arabic, but they would have broken Arabic. So the children, they would also learn this broken Arabic as well.
So those children who grew up in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], their Arabic was not as strong.
So the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], to prevent this problem from happening, when they would have sons,
they would prefer to send those children outside of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], in the middle of the desert,
so that they could grow up there with the Bedouins, and they could learn proper grammatical Arabic, [[fusha|فصحى]],
the beautiful, pure language of Arabic. So they would send their children outside for this purpose. This was one of the purposes. Another one
of the purposes was that life in the city is different than life outside
in the rural areas or in the desert. People who grow up in a city,
usually they grow up pampered, and they become soft when they grow up. So they didn't want their sons to grow up pampered and soft like that. They wanted
their children, their sons to develop this toughness, like real men.
So they thought it was better to send them outside into the desert so that they can have a little bit more of a difficult life
and they would grow up being tough and they would grow up as real men. So this was another one of the reasons they would send their children outside of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
So for the language,
to become tough, and the third reason was, like we said, so many people from different lands would come into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]],
and with them, they would bring different types of illnesses and different types of diseases. So the people staying in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], they would get sick a lot.
So to protect their children from being exposed to these type of illnesses, they would send them away.
And, you know, some of these things are still true about [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] today. There are so many people from outside who are there in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
And I have witnessed this myself. Sometimes some of the Arabs, the Saudis, when they're speaking to the people who are there from different countries,
they will speak to them with broken Arabic. Even though they know Arabic properly, they will still speak with them with a broken form of Arabic
so that it's easy for them to understand. So with this happening all the time, it really affects the total level of the language of the people. Also,

the sicknesses, of course, especially during [[Hajj|حج]] time, so many people are coming in, and you'll see a lot of different people with different types of sicknesses in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] during the days, especially, of [[Hajj|حج]].
So we can see where the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] were coming from and why they would send their children outside to have their initial upbringing. And then,
when they would grow up to a certain age, they would, of course, come back into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
So there were people from those deserts who would come into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] every once in a while
to search for children whose parents wanted to send them out into the desert. So these women
would come, they would come into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] searching for parents who have small children who want to give their children to be brought up in the desert.
And these women, they would also provide milk for these young children because the mothers are sending them away, so they're not going to be with their mother, but they still need their milk.
So there would be these women from the deserts who would come to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] to take these children back into the desert, and they would also provide them with their milk.
Now, it was from the custom of the Arabs that they would not agree upon a fee.
Like when these women would come from the desert and come into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] and take the children and give them milk and bring them up in the desert,
they would not agree on a fee for this service with the parents,
because they would consider this is something that is inappropriate. You know, "We're providing milk for the children and we're taking money for the milk?" This is not good.
They didn't think that that was culturally acceptable or appropriate. So they would not agree upon any type of fee for this.
But it was understood that after the period was up and when they would bring the children back to their parents in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], that the father
would give these women some type of a gift or some type of a token of their gratitude, and they would actually give them some money.
This was the habit, and this was
what was understood would happen, even though initially they would not agree upon a set fee.
So these women, they would come from the desert, and they would do this in order to earn a living.
You know, those women who were living in the deserts and their families, they were very poor.
So they would come into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] and take these children as a way to earn a living.
So once, when the Prophet ﷺ was born, the women from [[Banu Sa'd|بني سعد]]
came from the desert to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] to get the children to take into the desert to provide them with their milk and to bring them up in the desert.
So a group of women from [[Banu Sa'd|بني سعد]], and amongst these women was a woman named [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]], [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة السعدية]].
So they came into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] searching for these young boys to take into the desert to bring them up. Now [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]]
and her husband [[al-Harith|الحارث]], they were very, very poor. They were very, very poor. And [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]], she
had her own son. She had a son herself who was around the same age as [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ.
So she thought, "Okay, I will provide milk for my son and I will provide milk for another boy I get from [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] as well." But the thing is that
[[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]] was so poor,
and because of her poverty, she didn't have much to eat. She didn't have much nutrition herself.
So she didn't even produce enough milk to take care of her own son. Because she was so hungry herself, she wasn't even producing enough milk to fill up her own son.
But because she was so poor and she needed a way to earn some money,
she still decided to go into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] and try to find a boy that she could take with her as well, and hopefully, with [[barakah|بركة]], she would be able to
feed her son, and she will be able to feed this boy as well.
So the group of women from [[Banu Sa'd|بني سعد]], they come into [[Makkah|مكة]], and each one of them,
they find parents who want to give their son to be brought up in the desert, and many of the women, they go back with a boy.
But as for [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, his mother was trying to find someone who would take him as well, but everybody refused.
Everybody refused to take [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ.
And this was because he didn't have a father.
So they thought to themselves, you know, when we bring these boys back, the father is the one who gives us the money.
This boy doesn't have a father, so what are we going to get for taking care of him?
Yeah, his grandfather is there, his mother is there, but they are not going to be able to take care of us as if his father was alive.
So they were afraid to take him because they thought that they wouldn't get anything out of it.
So [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ was left, and the women, they went back into the deserts with other boys who were born around the same time.
Now [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]], she came into [[Makkah|مكة]] as well.
But she came a little bit later than the rest of the of the women from [[Banu Sa'd|بني سعد]].
And that was because, as we mentioned, she was very poor, and the donkey that she had that she used for transportation, it was an old, and it was a weak, and very slow donkey.
So she came later than the rest of them.
And when she came, at first she didn't take [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ either.
And they didn't find anyone else; [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]] and her husband, they didn't find any other boy to take.
So they were leaving [[Makkah|مكة]].
And when they were on the outskirts of [[Makkah|مكة]], [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]] said to her husband [[al-Harith|الحارث]],
she said to him, all of the other women, they took boys, but we came into [[Makkah|مكة]], now we're going to go back without anything.
You know what? I think we should go back into [[Makkah|مكة]], and we should take that boy, we should take that orphan boy.
And perhaps Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] will give us some [[barakah|بركة]], perhaps there will be some blessing in taking him.
him, and we will be taken care of as well. Let's just go, and let's take him.
So she made this decision which turned out to be the best and smartest decision in her life.
And they went back, and they took [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, and they took him back into the desert.
Now, the signs of the greatness of this baby were immediately visible.
Like we mentioned, when [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]] came from the desert into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], she came very slowly because her donkey was so weak and slow.
Now going back from [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] to the desert on that same donkey with [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, that donkey is going faster than any of the other animals
from the other people who were in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] who were going back as well. Now [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]]'s donkey is getting ahead of all of them.
Such to the extent that they asked her: 'Is this the same animal that you came in on?'
And she said: 'Yes, it's the same one.' And then they said: '[[Wallahi|والله]], there is something special about this. This is not normal.'
So that was the first sign of the [[barakah|بركة]], going from [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] back into the desert with such speed on this donkey that was previously so slow.
Also [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة]], who didn't have even enough milk to take care of her own son,
now that she has Muhammad ﷺ with her, she has more than enough milk to take care of her son and [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ and fill both of them up.
So these were the signs of the [[barakah|بركة]] of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ that came with him into that family, the family of [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة السعدية]].

So [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ grew up, he grew up in the desert with [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة السعدية]], and there were so many incidents and beautiful things that happened to him while he was there.
And [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]] we will talk about those incidents in our next session [[bi-idhnillah|بإذن الله]] next week.

segments.translit: Wallāhu aʿlam. Wa ṣallallāhu wa sallama wa bāraka ʿalā nabiyyinā Muḥammad wa ʿalā ālihi wa ṣaḥbihi ajmaʿīn.

review.q: Why did the Prophet ﷺ refer to himself as [[Ana ibnudh-dhabihayn|أنا ابن الذبيحين]]?
review.a: It refers to Ismail and [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله بن عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], whose sacrifice was averted when one hundred camels were offered in his place.

review.q: What significant event occurred in [[Yathrib|يثرب]] regarding the parents of the Prophet ﷺ?
review.a: [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله بن عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] and [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة بنت وهب]] were married there before returning to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].

review.q: What miraculous vision did [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة بنت وهب]] experience as the time of delivery approached?
review.a: She saw a light issuing from her that illuminated the palaces of [[Busra|بصرى]] in [[Sham|شام]].

review.q: When was [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] born according to the most authentic view?
review.a: On Monday, the 12th of [[Rabi al-Awwal|ربيع الأول]] in the [[Am al-Fil|عام الفيل]], fifty days after the destruction of [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]]'s army.

review.q: What physical signs were recorded at the birth of the Prophet ﷺ?
review.a: He was born circumcised and with his umbilical cord already detached.

review.q: What three main purposes did the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] custom of desert upbringing serve?
review.a: Mastering pure Arabic ([[fusha|فصحى]]), developing physical strength and toughness, and avoiding diseases from international pilgrims.

review.q: Why did [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة السعدية]] decide to take the infant Prophet ﷺ when other wet nurses rejected him?
review.a: She accepted the orphan in hopes of divine blessing ([[barakah|بركة]]) after finding no other child.

review.q: What lesson does the speaker draw from [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة السعدية]] taking the orphan Prophet ﷺ?
review.a: Seeking divine blessing through good deeds yields far greater rewards than chasing immediate material gain.
